entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
The delay in filing the counter affidavit is condoned.
Counter affidavit is taken on record.
Delay Condonation Application (IA) No.1 of 2023, stands disposed of accordingly.
2. Applicant Sher Ali is in judicial custody FIR/Case Crime No.518 of 2023, dated 15.06.2023, under Sections 376(2)(n), 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Laksar, District Haridwar.
He has sought his release on bail.

3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
4.
According to the FIR, the applicant and the victim, both were known to each other for the four years from the date of lodging of the FIR.
The FIR records that once the applicant took the victim at a place and raped her.
Thereafter, he continued raping her under threat.
He also pressurized the victim to change her religion or else threatened her to life.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the victim is a major girl; the relationship was consensual; they were in relationship, but due to the difference in religion they could not marry;
it is thereafter that under the pressure of her family, the victim has lodged an FIR.

sentences.text:
It is also argued that there is no date, place of alleged incident for four years the victim kept mum;
she did not raise any alarm.
7. Learned State counsel would submit that the victim was threatened by the applicant in the name of videos and photographs viral.
8. The Court wanted to know from the learned State counsel, as to whether any such videos or photographs were ever recovered by the Investigating Officer?
He would submit that there are no such videos or photographs available.
9. Admittedly, the victim did not raise ever any alarm for the complete four years.
According to the FIR also, initially their meetings were convenient for both, the victim and the applicant.
The birth year of the victim is 1998, as recorded in the FIR.
10. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
11. The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
13.
Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 15.03.2024 Sanjay Sher Ali vs State Of Uttarakhand on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154849277/
